o.c: Butter is mostly fat, so mixed with whole milk it stands in for heavy cream at 3 parts milk to 1 part butter. Closest in richness.
o.st: Melt the extra butter, whisk in the milk, then simmer gently until it thickens slightly.

o.c: Evaporated milk contains a lot of fat, which makes it a good substitute, though it adds a slight caramelized flavor.
o.st: Pour in the evaporated milk and simmer gently until it thickens slightly.

o.c: Oil is all fat, so mixed with soy milk it stands in for heavy cream at 2 parts milk to 1 part oil. Lactose free and vegan.
o.st: Whisk the oil into the soy milk, pour it in, and simmer gently without boiling hard.

o.c: Thick, unsweetened coconut cream swaps 1:1 in sauces, soups and desserts with a mild coconut flavor. Chill a can overnight and scoop off the solids if you need to whip it.
Half-and-half has a similar texture and fat content. It is slightly richer, and is likely the best evaporated milk substitute.
Simmer the milk on the stove for about 30 minutes, until it has reduced by about 60%.
Rises and bakes like self-rising flour as long as the baking powder is whisked in evenly. Skip any extra baking powder or salt in your recipe.
Flour thickens like cornstarch with slightly different properties. Whisk it into cold water first. It takes about 2 minutes longer to thicken.
Swap 1:1. Thickens at a lower temperature and stays glossy, but turns slimy with dairy and doesn't reheat well.
Swap 1:1. Stir it in at the end and don't boil it, or it breaks down.
Tapioca is a weaker thickener, so use twice as much. Gives a glossy finish that holds up to freezing.
Honey is sweeter than sugar, so use about three-quarters as much. Cut other liquid in the recipe by roughly 1/4 cup per cup of honey and lower the oven by 25°F, since honey browns faster.
Swap 1:1, packed. Adds a light molasses flavor and a slightly moister, chewier result.
Use three-quarters as much and cut other liquid by about 3 tablespoons per cup of syrup. Adds a mild maple flavor.
Agave is sweeter than sugar, so use about two-thirds as much. Cut other liquid by about 1/4 cup per cup of sugar replaced and lower the oven by 25°F.
Swap 1:1. Slightly less sweet, with a caramel flavor and a darker color.
Rub 1 tablespoon of molasses into each cup of white sugar for light brown sugar. Use 2 tablespoons for dark brown sugar.
Swap 1:1. Slightly drier than brown sugar, with a caramel flavor.
Thinner and milder than honey. Swap 1:1.
Mild and a little thinner than honey. Swap 1:1 for a lighter flavor.
A similar sticky sweetness. Swap 1:1.
Fine sea salt measures about the same as table salt. Swap 1:1 and season to taste.
Kosher salt has larger flakes, so it takes more by volume. Use 1 1/2 times as much for Morton, or twice as much for Diamond Crystal.
Table salt is denser than kosher salt, so use about two-thirds as much for Morton, or half as much for Diamond Crystal.
Fine sea salt measures like table salt. Use about two-thirds as much for Morton kosher, or half for Diamond Crystal.

Oil is all fat while butter is about 80% fat, so use three-quarters as much. Works in savory dishes, cakes, muffins and quick breads, but it won't cream or flake like butter, so skip it for cookies and pastry.
Solid coconut oil behaves a lot like butter in baking and creaming. Swap 1:1. Refined has a neutral taste; unrefined tastes of coconut.
Swap 1:1 using stick margarine. Many brands contain milk solids, so check the label if you need it lactose free.
Swap 1:1 for tender baked goods and flaky pastry, but without the buttery flavor.
A neutral oil for sautéing, roasting and baking. You lose the fruity, peppery olive flavor.
Good for sautéing and roasting. Butter browns faster, so use medium heat. Not suited to raw uses like dressings.
Use melted refined coconut oil for a neutral taste.
Swap 1:1. Choose a light or mild olive oil for baking so it doesn't overpower.
Melt and cool slightly. Gives a richer, buttery flavor, though butter is part water so the crumb is a touch less moist.
Keeps bakes moist with less fat. Best in muffins, quick breads and cakes; the crumb is denser and browns less.
Use melted coconut oil. Refined has a neutral taste; unrefined tastes of coconut.
Richer and creamier than milk. Swap 1:1, or thin with a splash of water for a lighter result.
Equal parts evaporated milk and water make a good stand-in for whole milk, with a slightly richer, cooked-milk flavor.
Use unsweetened almond milk in savory dishes. It's thinner and milder than dairy, so sauces may take longer to thicken.
Use the thin, drinkable coconut milk sold in cartons, not the canned kind. Adds a faint coconut flavor.
Swap 1:1 using unsweetened soy milk. It has the most protein of the plant milks, so it behaves best in baking and sauces.
Swap 1:1 using unsweetened oat milk. Creamy and slightly sweet.
A slightly softer, lower-fat cream cheese with a near-identical taste. Swap 1:1.
Richer, sweeter and less tangy. Works well in frostings, cheesecakes and dips.
Whisk the ground flaxseed into the water and let it sit about 5 minutes until gel-like. Works in cookies, muffins, pancakes and quick breads, but not where eggs are the star.
Adds moisture and some binding to muffins, quick breads and cakes. It adds no lift, so use it where the recipe has other leavening.
Adds moisture and binding along with a banana flavor. Best in pancakes, muffins and quick breads.
Stir the chia seeds into the water and let sit about 10 minutes until gel-like. Works like a flax egg in muffins, cookies and pancakes.
The liquid from a can of chickpeas. Whisk lightly before using. Good in cakes, brownies and pancakes.
Blend until completely smooth first. Adds moisture and body to dense cakes, brownies and quick breads.
Whisk both into the dry ingredients and bake right away. Make only what the recipe needs.
Higher protein gives a chewier, firmer result. Swap 1:1.
Cake flour is lighter, so use about 2 extra tablespoons per cup. Gives a softer, more tender crumb.
Nuttier and denser. For the lightest result, swap half the flour and keep the rest all-purpose.
Use a cup-for-cup blend that already contains xanthan gum. Batters often need a few minutes' rest to hydrate.
Swap 1:1. Adds the tiny black vanilla seeds too.
Almond extract is stronger than vanilla, so use half as much. Gives a nutty, cherry-like flavor.
Adds a mild, caramel-like sweetness. Trim a little sugar elsewhere if you can.
Split the pod and scrape out the seeds. One bean equals about 1 tablespoon of extract.
Usually made without wheat, so it's the go-to gluten-free swap. Slightly richer and less salty.
Milder, sweeter and lower in sodium. Add a pinch of salt to taste.
Swap 1:1. Slightly sharper and more floral.
Vinegar is more acidic and has no citrus flavor, so use half as much. Better in dressings, marinades and sauces than in desserts.
Milder and sweeter, so you may want to cut a little sugar elsewhere. Best in baking and glazes.
About 1/8 teaspoon of garlic powder equals one clove. Stir it into liquid or add it with the dry seasonings so it doesn't scorch.
About 1/2 teaspoon of jarred minced garlic equals one clove. Milder than fresh.
Milder and a touch sweeter than onion. Swap chopped shallot 1:1.
Use the well-washed white and light-green parts. Mild and sweet; cook until soft.
About 1 tablespoon of onion powder replaces one medium onion (roughly 1 cup chopped). Gives flavor but no texture.
Milder and fresher. Use the white and green parts, and add them near the end of cooking.
Lighter and a little sweeter. Add an extra pinch of salt to taste.
Deeper, richer flavor. Better in stews, gravies and hearty soups than in delicate dishes.
Dissolve 1 teaspoon of bouillon granules (or 1 cube) in each cup of hot water. Bouillon is salty, so go light on added salt.
The broth adds savory depth and the vinegar replaces the acidity. Good for deglazing and sauces.
Sweeter than wine, so the vinegar matters. Best in glazes, light sauces and desserts.
A drop-in swap that's a bit more herbal. It still contains alcohol.
Milder and grassy rather than citrusy. Add a squeeze of lime juice for a brighter, cilantro-like note.
Same color with a deeper, smoky flavor. Swap 1:1.
A blend that adds mild heat plus cumin and garlic notes. Swap 1:1.
Much hotter and adds heat rather than color. Start with a quarter of the amount and add to taste.
Already contains cinnamon plus ginger, nutmeg and clove. Swap 1:1 for a warmer, more complex flavor.
A cinnamon-forward blend with nutmeg and allspice. Swap 1:1.
Warm and slightly peppery with a hint of clove. Swap 1:1.
Mace comes from the same fruit as nutmeg and tastes very similar, just a little more delicate. Swap 1:1.
A blend with cinnamon, ginger and clove along with nutmeg. Swap 1:1.
Stir the lemon juice into the milk and let it stand 5 minutes until slightly curdled. Use a scant cup of milk if you want it exact.
Whisk the yogurt and milk together until smooth and pourable.
Whisk the sour cream and milk together until smooth and pourable.
Stir the lemon juice into unsweetened soy milk and let it stand 5 minutes until it thickens slightly.
Thick and tangy. Swap 1:1; full-fat works best, and stir it in off the heat so it doesn't curdle.
Richer and a little less tangy, and it won't curdle in hot dishes. Swap 1:1.
Soften the cream cheese and whisk in a splash of milk until it's the texture of sour cream.
A little richer and less tangy. Swap 1:1.
Strain regular plain yogurt through cheesecloth or a coffee filter for an hour or two until it's thick.
Use unsweetened coconut yogurt. Dairy free, with a mild coconut flavor.
Chill a can overnight and scoop off the thick cream that rises to the top.
Swap 1:1 for a dairy version of the same richness.
Equal parts milk and cream is exactly what half-and-half is.
Melt the butter and whisk it into the milk.
Slightly less rich, with a cooked-milk flavor. Swap 1:1.
Tangier and lighter. Swap 1:1 in dressings, dips and salads.
Tangy and creamy. Swap 1:1 in dips, dressings and salads.
Drain it, and blend it if you want a smooth texture like ricotta.
Creamier and milder. Swap 1:1.
Saltier and sharper, so go easy on added salt.
Aged asiago is nutty and close to Parmesan.
Very similar to Parmesan, a little milder and softer.
Melts well with a little more flavor.
Mild and melty. Swap 1:1.
Milder and softer than cheddar, but it melts the same way.
Blend in a blender or spice grinder until powdery. The cornstarch stops it from clumping.
Swap 1:1. Honey is a little sweeter, with a floral flavor.
Swap 1:1 for a milder, thinner sweetness.
Swap 1:1 for a thinner syrup with maple flavor. Not suited to candy-making.
Swap 1:1. Very similar in texture and sweetness.
Baking powder is weaker, so use three times as much. Cut back on any added salt, and expect a slightly different flavor.
Use 2 teaspoons per teaspoon of cream of tartar to stabilize whipped egg whites.
Use 2 teaspoons per teaspoon of cream of tartar to stabilize whipped egg whites.
One vanilla pod is about 1 tablespoon of extract. Add it near the end of cooking.
One vanilla pod is about 1 tablespoon of paste, and the paste includes the seeds.
Whips up like egg white. Use the liquid from a can of chickpeas.
Whisk the powder into the water first. Works for meringue and royal icing.
Crush plain crackers finely. Swap by weight.
Pulse rolled oats in a blender until crumbly. Swap by weight.
Swap by weight.
Swap 1:1. Butter adds flavor but spreads more in cookies.
Swap 1:1 using stick margarine. Check the label if you need it lactose free.
Solid coconut oil acts like shortening. Refined has a neutral taste.
Naturally sweeter and caffeine free, with a milder, earthier flavor.
A little sweeter. Swap by weight.
Less sweet, with a stronger almond flavor. Swap by weight and add a little sugar if needed.
Sweeter and tangier. Fine in a pinch for sauces and braises.
Simmer the sauce down until thick and cut other liquid in the recipe to match.
Swap 1:1. Slightly thinner and more seasoned.
Whisk equal parts paste and water until smooth.
Sharper and more complex. Swap 1:1.
Milder and tangier. Swap 1:1.
Sharper, so add a pinch of sugar to balance it.
Fruitier and a little stronger. Swap 1:1.
Slightly sharper. Swap 1:1.
Sweeter and darker. Swap 1:1.
Fruitier and a touch milder. Swap 1:1.
Lighter in color and flavor. Swap 1:1.
Swap 1:1. Slightly less sharp and more sweet.
Sweeter and tropical. Swap 1:1.
Milder and sweeter, with less acidity. Swap 1:1.
Sweeter and thicker, with less savory depth. Swap 1:1.
Stir the sugar into the soy sauce for a salty-sweet stand-in.
Less pungent. Add a squeeze of lime juice for brightness.
Sweeter and thicker. Swap 1:1.
Saltier and less tangy. Add a drop of vinegar if you have it.
The closest common stand-in. Swap 1:1.
Lighter and a little sweeter. Swap 1:1.
Whisk equal parts coconut cream and water until smooth.
Richer and more savory. Swap 1:1.
Stronger and sweeter. Use smooth, unsweetened.
Milder and slightly sweet. Swap 1:1.
Nut free and close in flavor. Swap 1:1.
Milder and a little less sweet. Swap 1:1.
Nut free. Swap 1:1.
More bitter and savory. Add a little sugar if needed.
Stronger than shallot. Swap 1:1 and cook a little longer to mellow it.
Sharper when raw but sweet once cooked. Swap 1:1.
Milder and fresher. Add near the end of cooking.
Milder and more delicate. Add at the end.
Sweeter and a little sharper. Swap 1:1.
Sharper. Use less if eating raw.
Much more tender, so cook it for less time.
Tougher and a little milder. Cook a bit longer.
Cooks faster, so shorten the cooking time.
Nutty and high in protein. Cook until the little tails pop out.
Chewy and hearty. Pearled barley cooks in about 30 minutes.
Drier, with separate grains. Swap 1:1.
Grate fresh ginger. About 1 tablespoon replaces 1 teaspoon of ground. Brighter and sharper.
Works in baking. Warm and sweet with a hint of clove.
Contains cumin along with mild chile and garlic. Swap 1:1.
A warm blend that includes cumin. Swap 1:1.
Milder and grassy. Add a little lemon zest to echo dill's brightness.
Cooler and sweeter. Works best in yogurt and cucumber dishes.
A little hotter and earthier, with no black flecks. Swap 1:1.
Much hotter and adds heat, not black pepper's bite. Start with a quarter and taste.
Finer and hotter than flakes. Start with a quarter of the amount and taste.
A blend of cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg and clove. Swap 1:1.
Warm and nutty. Swap 1:1.
Earthier and a little stronger. Swap 1:1.
A blend that includes thyme. Swap 1:1.
A blend of sage, thyme and marjoram. Great with chicken and stuffing.
A blend that includes oregano. Swap 1:1.
Milder and more lemony. Swap 1:1.
Sweeter and more delicate, and the closest relative. Swap 1:1.
Gentler and less piney. Swap 1:1.
Earthy and peppery. Use a little less if it's very fresh.
A blend where sage is the main flavor. Swap 1:1.
Piney and strong. Use a little less and chop it fine.
Milder and earthy. Swap 1:1.
